races.name: Sheahan's Pharmacy 3-Y-O Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Another Day Done
runners_data.note: Flat form over 7-10f on good/standard, and the step to 2m1f hurdles is a significant unknown; a genuine hold-up horse whose position in the race map overstates how close she'll actually race, and with only one win from eight runs and 83 days off the track, she carries plenty of questions.

runners_data.name: Camp Verde
runners_data.note: Finished 12th on debut over hurdles 10 days ago and her form string carries a fade flag — a natural closer who has yet to show the staying quality this 2m1f trip demands; likely to be ridden from well off the pace but finding the straight too short for a meaningful late challenge.

runners_data.name: Chairmanforlife
runners_data.note: Mark Walsh in the saddle for Mrs John Harrington is a strong pairing, and a P-style horse who has run consistently at 10-13f on good ground is well-suited positionally; two runs at this course/going profile and no wins, but the form figures are honest and the trainer fires at 2/31 over 14 days.

runners_data.name: Connor Of Mali
runners_data.note: A troubled record — pulled up and unseated in recent starts over hurdles — makes this horse difficult to assess; his natural hold-up style means he'll race further back than the map places him, and the fade flag compounds the concern about his finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Divelment
runners_data.note: Wearing a hood and ridden by Philip Byrnes, this horse has run eight times since last June without winning; a genuine hold-up type who sits further back than his mapped position implies, and while he picked up one placed effort on standard going, good turf hasn't yielded a result.

runners_data.name: Harmani
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy takes the ride for Gordon Elliott, whose stable is 4/35 in the past 14 days — the premier booking in the race; won on good going over 10f and was placed over 8f on soft, suggesting he handles the ground and the yard fits the profile for a prominent racer who can quicken late.

runners_data.name: Manntari
runners_data.note: Tom Kelly (7lb claimer) rides for E McNamara, who is 0/3 in the 14-day window; only one run over hurdles — seventh of 12 over good ground — and with minimal information available, the natural hold-up style means he's unlikely to be anywhere near the front despite the map.

runners_data.name: Minella Buoy
runners_data.note: The most consistent hold-up performer in the field with back-to-back seconds over this sort of trip and going, wearing a hood; the closest thing to a proven stayer among the closers, and the one most likely to be genuinely aimed late rather than just mapped there by default.

runners_data.name: Guildhall Graduate
runners_data.note: Five runs in the good-going sim profile without a win or place, and a rating of 147lbs suggests Kevin Sexton faces a tough task; the hold-up style means he needs pace to build into, and with Sea Of Dubka likely to keep it honest rather than suicidal, a late challenge is structurally difficult.

runners_data.name: Misty Cove
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell sends this one out wearing a tongue tie, and the trainer is in form at 5/16 over 14 days; a P-style horse who won on soft going and was placed twice, she steps back to good ground which she handles, and sitting just off Sea Of Dubka's shoulder suits her profile.

runners_data.name: Sea Of Dubka
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's runner is the only confirmed front-runner in the race and has won over 13f on good going; Darragh O'Keeffe rides and will dictate terms uncontested, making this the horse around whom all tactical decisions revolve — the key question is whether she can sustain the gallop over 2m1f hurdles.

races.paceDynamic: Sea Of Dubka is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no serious challenger for the lead, will control this 2m1f maiden hurdle from the outset at Killarney on good ground, setting a measured, uncontested gallop that favours a horse who can travel prominently and attack from the front. Chairmanforlife, Harmani, and Misty Cove are the natural prominent racers who will track Sea Of Dubka and be best placed entering the straight. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can naturally accommodate — Divelment, Connor Of Mali, Camp Verde, Guildhall Graduate, Minella Buoy, Another Day Done, and Manntari are all true closers, but with so many genuine hold-up horses in the field, several will be unable to get their preferred position and may end up racing closer than ideal or further back in a congested midfield; the most likely beneficiaries of the true back positions are Minella Buoy, who has shown consistency, and Guildhall Graduate. A sustainable, single-paced lead from Sea Of Dubka with a small cluster pressing from prominent positions creates an ideal setup for prominent racers who stay the trip — this race shape most favours P-style horses with stamina, as closers will face a flat, honest gallop that gives no natural compression to exploit late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sea Of Dubka Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Sea Of Dubka bowls along unchallenged and the prominent horses cannot sustain a challenge turning in.
scenarios.body: Sea Of Dubka dictates on her own terms at a steady-to-fair gallop, and horses who track her closely — Harmani, Chairmanforlife, Misty Cove — are best positioned to challenge; with a lone leader setting an honest but not suicidal pace on good ground, the winner is likely to come from the front two or three.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Sea Of Dubka fades from the front in the closing stages and the tracking prominent horses sweep past.
scenarios.body: Harmani and Chairmanforlife, sitting second and third throughout, are ideally placed to collar a tiring leader at the final hurdle; Harmani's prior Flat win on good ground and Jack Kennedy's positioning give this profile real credibility if the pace has been just firm enough to blunt Sea Of Dubka.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Consistent Closer Hits
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to create a true finishing opportunity for a hold-up horse in the final 2f.
scenarios.body: Minella Buoy's two consecutive second-place finishes over this sort of trip suggest she's the closest to a genuine stayer among the hold-up brigade, and she is the most likely beneficiary if closers find daylight late; however, this scenario depends on the pace being stronger than a single front-runner typically generates, making it the least structurally supported shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Implodes Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses mid-race and several horses trade positions chaotically in a slowly-run contest that becomes a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A muddling gallop set by Sea Of Dubka could theoretically compress the field and bring hold-up horses into contention earlier than expected, but the structural absence of pace rivals makes a true sprint finish unlikely on this track; if it does materialise, Harmani's Flat pace and Misty Cove's headgear (tongue tie) could prove decisive.

watchPoints.text: Sea Of Dubka sets the entire pace structure alone — if she jumps well and travels easily, she could prove very difficult to peg back, making her jump at the first and early fluency the single most important moment of the race.

Harmani and Chairmanforlife are both prominent types competing for the same ground behind the leader — watch how Kennedy and Walsh place their horses leaving the first bend, as a scrimmage for position between these two could compromise one or both.

Minella Buoy is the most credible hold-up threat but must find a clean run turning into the straight — with several horses mapped to midfield who are naturally hold-up types, traffic congestion in the home turn is a genuine risk for the closers.

Connor Of Mali's record of falls and pull-ups in recent starts is a race-safety concern in a 11-runner field — Phillip Enright should be monitored for any jumping hesitancy at the early hurdles that could affect horses tracking closely.

The trainer-in-form angle of Gavin Cromwell (5/16 in 14 days) applies to both Misty Cove and Guildhall Graduate — if either shows unexpected improvement, the yard's current strike rate suggests it should not be dismissed purely on bare form figures.

races.name: GMIB Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Fiveonefive
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator with a recent course win over 17f on Good and promising sim-going stats (10/15), but Jack Kennedy must navigate from the rear in a field where hold-up horses are competing for a small amount of late racing room; the 19-day turnaround is fine and the headgear (p) has been worn before.
runners_data.comment: Fiveonefive advertises his fitness with a win last time out, just 19 days ago, and has run over today's trip and going before, giving him solid grounding for conditions; the 166 lb burden is the one weight he must shoulder, but his recent upswing in form makes him our pick.

runners_data.name: Autumn Twist
runners_data.note: Prominent racer ideally suited to tracking a lone front-runner; her recent 2nd over this course and distance on Good is the standout piece of form in the race, and Daniel King's low-key booking shouldn't mask what is a strong positional profile today.
runners_data.comment: Autumn Twist shapes as a genuine threat here, having run over today's trip and going before and returning on a fresh 21-day break carrying 161 lb; a second last time out is an obvious strength, though winless in his last five starts remains the key concern.

runners_data.name: Feud
runners_data.note: 214 days off the track is a significant concern, and a recent form string of P090F is alarming — while the sim-going record (10/15) is acceptable and Sean Flanagan is a competent partner, fitness and consistency must be questioned before confidence is placed.
runners_data.comment: Rated highest in the field and carrying 161 lb, Feud has run over today's trip and going before, and his class makes him a genuine threat despite being winless in recent starts; the chief concern is a fall last time out followed by a 214-day absence.

runners_data.name: Hi Ho Idaho
runners_data.note: The race's sole front-runner, and that is his biggest asset today — a consecutive-form line of 3332-1 including a win over 20f on Good shows he stays well and has found winning form; Danny Gilligan should have him beautifully positioned to dictate from the front without a rival to force the pace.
runners_data.comment: Consistent in recent starts with a win and three thirds in his last five, Hi Ho Idaho arrives on going he has encountered before; however, 101 days off the track is a notable fitness query, and 155 lb is a stiff weight to overcome on a comeback.

runners_data.name: Black Bamboo
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up type returning after 214 days off with a form string dominated by double-digit finishes; Donagh Meyler has no yard support (T14: 0/0) and the sim-going record (8/15) is modest — this profile carries serious questions.
runners_data.comment: Black Bamboo has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 130 ranks him third among these ten, making him a serious threat on that measure; the main risk is a string of unplaced efforts in recent starts and 214 days off the track.

runners_data.name: Gino Bella
runners_data.note: Two consecutive wins at 17f on Good, headgear (ht) presumably retained, and Alan O'Sullivan's 5lb claim reduces the burden — a prominent racing style means he is well placed to stalk the pace and could be underestimated at a lower OR of 115.
runners_data.comment: Ranked ninth of ten on our figures, Gino Bella faces a stiff task at the weights carrying 150 lb, yet her recent form is genuinely eye-catching — back-to-back wins in her last two starts, and she has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Fast Felix
runners_data.note: Consistent handler of Good ground (14/15 sim-going runs), but his true style is hold-up racing; placed into the midfield map due to overcrowding at the rear, he faces the likelihood of racing away from his natural position, which tempers confidence even with decent recent form.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in his last five starts, and a pulled-up effort five runs back remains a concern, Fast Felix has experience over today's trip and conditions in his favour, though carrying 149 lb from a midfield ranking makes this a stiff task.

runners_data.name: Moylussa
runners_data.note: Three-time runner who has placed twice at 16f on Good and is handled by Darragh O'Keeffe, a positive booking — yet this horse's genuine instinct is to race from behind, and with the rear of the field already overcrowded, securing a clean passage to deliver a late run is far from guaranteed.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked eighth of ten on our figures, Moylussa is hard to fancy at first glance, though back-to-back thirds and experience over today's trip and going offer slim encouragement; the 73-day absence is another question mark.

runners_data.name: Lord Ffrench
runners_data.note: Phillip Enright has course experience but this horse's entire profile screams hold-up racing, and a form string of 76-867 with no win offers little encouragement; like the other pushed-forward hold-up types, racing out of role in a pace-controlled race is a significant handicap.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with finishes no better than sixth in recent outings, Lord Ffrench faces a stiff ask ranked last on our figures here; he has run over today's trip and going, and 22 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh, but that may be his strongest claim.

runners_data.name: Eye Contact
runners_data.note: Twice placed at 18f on Good and just 17 days since last run, which suggests fitness is fine — but this is another natural hold-up horse forced into the midfield map, and with headgear (tp) and an OR of just 104, the task of producing a winning run from an uncomfortable position is steep.
runners_data.comment: Consistent without converting, Eye Contact has finished second in each of his last two starts and has run over today's trip and going before, though winless in his last five and a demanding 140 lb to shoulder may test his resolution.

races.paceDynamic: Hi Ho Idaho is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival pressing for the lead, Danny Gilligan can dictate a measured, controlled gallop from the front — a significant positional advantage over 2m1f on Good ground at Killarney. Autumn Twist and Gino Bella are the two prominent types most likely to sit just behind Hi Ho Idaho and track the tempo, with Autumn Twist's recent 2nd over course and distance giving her a strong claims to secure that position. The field is deceptively hold-up heavy: Fast Felix, Moylussa, Lord Ffrench, and Eye Contact are all genuine hold-up horses who have been pushed into the midfield map because the rear is overcrowded — they are unlikely to find their natural hunting ground, which compromises their chance in a shape that demands a late run. With a single pace-setter setting a comfortable tempo and the bulk of the field unable to get their preferred position, this race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can track the front-runner and pounce from a close-up pitch before the hold-up horses can mount a meaningful challenge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hi Ho Idaho Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Hi Ho Idaho bowls along uncontested and sets a fair but not punishing gallop, allowing his prominent followers to race within themselves.
scenarios.body: Hi Ho Idaho, fresh off a win over 20f on Good and handled by an in-form stable, is gifted a dream scenario with no rival to stretch him — he or a close tracker simply outstays the field in the straight. Prominent horses Autumn Twist and Gino Bella, both suited by Good ground and positioned right behind the pace, are best placed to capitalise as hold-up types fail to close from too far back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Hi Ho Idaho sets enough gallop to cut out the race but is collared approaching the last by an organised prominent racer sitting just off the pace.
scenarios.body: Autumn Twist, with a recent 2nd over this exact course and distance on Good, is ideally placed to track and overhaul a front-runner who has done the donkey work; Gino Bella, carrying headgear and back-to-back wins at 17f on Good, poses a similar threat from a similar pitch. This shape rewards horses who had a clean passage throughout rather than those forced wide or deep from a hold-up position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Lucky Run
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or traffic breaks open a late gap that allows a genuine hold-up horse to thread through and arrive with a rattle.
scenarios.body: This is only plausible if the early tempo is truly modest and a redistribution horse like Fast Felix or Fiveonefive finds an unusual clear passage — both conditions are uncertain given the crowded rear and controlled pace. Fast Felix has course-form over this trip on Good and Fiveonefive won over this distance recently, but both are swimming against the tactical current today.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse — Chaos Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Hi Ho Idaho goes off too fast for the conditions and capitulates before the last, scrambling the race wide open.
scenarios.body: A genuine meltdown of the front-runner would theoretically let the midfield horses arrive in a heap, but given the absence of pace pressure and Gilligan's likely restraint, this is a low-probability event. Even in this shape, Autumn Twist and Gino Bella — who have been prominent without over-racing — are better positioned to benefit than true hold-up types stuck further back.

watchPoints.text: Hi Ho Idaho is the single pace-setter — if he quickens early or is pushed wider than expected out of the gate, the entire race shape changes and prominent trackers lose their reference point.

Autumn Twist's recent course-and-distance second on Good is the form pick for this shape, but watch whether Daniel King elects to sit tight behind Hi Ho Idaho or drifts back into the hold-up pack — positioning in the first two furlongs will be decisive.

Fast Felix, Moylussa, Lord Ffrench and Eye Contact are all genuine hold-up horses mapped to midfield — if they bunch together approaching the final bend and create a traffic jam, none may get a clear run even if the pace is right for them.

Gino Bella carries headgear (ht) and has won back-to-back at this trip on Good; if Alan O'Sullivan (5lb claimer) is confident enough to sit third or fourth early, that claim and positional advantage could make him a dangerous each-way runner.

Feud's 214-day absence and erratic recent form (P090F) makes him an unpredictable factor — if he jumps fluently and races prominently off the pace, his historical Good-ground record (10/15) could make him an unexpectedly live presence, but fitness on comeback must be monitored.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Novice Hurdle

runners_data.name: Loch Cuan
runners_data.note: A consistent prominent racer with two wins and two places from five starts on Good going, including back-to-back wins at 2m6f+; James Smith's claim is useful and the 55-day break for Gordon Elliott — who is 4/35 in the past 14 days — is not a concern given a yard in form.

runners_data.name: Brother Walfrid
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the field and likely to dictate from flag to finish under Jack Kennedy; headgear fitted, has won at this sort of trip before, and his 1/19f on Good ground suggests the conditions are no issue — the key question is whether his stamina holds over 2m7f.

runners_data.name: Don Jefe
runners_data.note: In reality a hold-up horse whose natural style is rear-of-field, though the map places him in midfield as the race shape is unlikely to create a true waiting opportunity; a 137-day absence since a pulled-up run, inconsistent form figures, and a modest trainer strike rate of 1/8 in the past fortnight add to the concerns.

runners_data.name: Local News
runners_data.note: Two from two under rules, both wins on Good ground (1/24f and 1/19f), giving him an outstanding profile on conditions and trip; held up naturally, so his chance depends on the pace being genuine enough to close into — Josh Williamson's 3lb claim is a small bonus.

runners_data.name: Diamond Du Berlais
runners_data.note: Top-rated in the field at OR 131 and trained by Mullins, but his Good-ground figures (3/15 in similar conditions, no wins) are a red flag and he has finished out of the first three in four of his last five starts; Brian Hayes keeps the ride, but this runner needs to dramatically reverse recent course-going form.

runners_data.name: Pets Georgina
runners_data.note: Has won twice and placed twice from seven starts on Good ground, including a recent win at 2m3f and a win at 2m4f, making the step up to 2m7f the primary unknown; J J Slevin's booking for a yard not in its sharpest 14-day form is worth noting, and her prominent style suits this pace map well.

races.paceDynamic: Brother Walfrid is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with Jack Kennedy in the saddle for Gordon Elliott, will dictate from the front at a sustainable clip over this 2m7f trip on Good ground. Loch Cuan and Pets Georgina will press forward into prominent positions, sitting just off the leader and ensuring the race is not entirely without early pressure, though neither is likely to directly challenge Brother Walfrid for the lead. The hold-up trio of Local News, Diamond Du Berlais, and Don Jefe will be ridden from the rear, though with Brother Walfrid controlling a manageable tempo this field will almost certainly race in a compressed bunch for much of the journey, limiting the advantage for pure closers. This race shape — a single, uncontested front-runner setting a measured pace on Good ground over a stamina trip — strongly favours horses that can travel prominently or just off the pace and produce a sustained run from the second-last, rather than those needing a strong gallop to close into. The field holds more hold-up types than can all benefit from a true end-to-end test; Don Jefe, a genuine rear-of-field operator, has been redistributed to midfield in the map as the shape is unlikely to accommodate a true waiting ride.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Brother Walfrid Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Brother Walfrid bowls along at a measured pace and the prominent horses are unable to reel him in from the second-last.
scenarios.body: Kennedy dictates every yard from the front, setting just enough pace to soften the closers without emptying himself, and the hold-up horses find the tempo too controlled to make meaningful ground on the leaders approaching the last two flights. Prominent runners who travel smoothly in his slipstream, particularly Loch Cuan and Pets Georgina, are ideally placed to pick off Brother Walfrid only if he ties up, but the front-runner's stamina profile over this trip makes him the primary beneficiary.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Swamp Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Loch Cuan or Pets Georgina apply sustained pressure from three out and grind down Brother Walfrid in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: The early pace set by Brother Walfrid proves just enough to stretch the hold-up horses but not enough to shake off two prominent chasers, and whichever of Loch Cuan or Pets Georgina travels best into the straight produces the decisive move at the second-last. Both have winning form on Good going at comparable trips and their jockeys — James Smith and J J Slevin respectively — are capable of timing a run to perfection in a small field.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Spring Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely strong enough to create a truly run race and the closers find daylight to deliver a late challenge.
scenarios.body: Local News is the most interesting hold-up runner here, unbeaten in two starts on Good ground and likely to be produced with a well-timed late run by Josh Williamson, while Diamond Du Berlais offers class on paper but must improve markedly on recent Good-ground form. This scenario requires a stronger gallop than Brother Walfrid is likely to set as a lone leader, which materially reduces its probability.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart — Errors Decide
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or a false pace causes the race to dissolve into a sprint finish from the last flight.
scenarios.body: Brother Walfrid carries headgear and any jumping lapse from him could bungle the pace plan entirely, leaving the race open to whoever avoids trouble, with Don Jefe's hold-up style — though unlikely to get a true waiting ride in this shape — potentially suiting a chaotic finale. This scenario is low-probability given Good ground and an experienced front-runner, but the small field and multiple jumps novices make a scrambled finish a non-zero risk.

watchPoints.text: Brother Walfrid sets the sole pace and any jumping error or unexpected loss of jumping rhythm from him would directly disrupt the race shape — watch him at every flight, particularly the downhill hurdles.

Local News is unbeaten in two runs and clearly unexposed; if Josh Williamson gets a smooth passage from the rear and the pace is even marginally stronger than expected, Local News could arrive late with a winning run that catches the eye.

Diamond Du Berlais is officially the classiest runner but has been beaten on Good ground repeatedly — if he travels easily for Mullins and Hayes, he represents a place threat, but his form makes a serious winning challenge difficult to trust.

Don Jefe's 137-day absence combined with being pushed out of his natural hold-up role means his peak performance today is genuinely unlikely — monitor his jumping early as a gauge of whether he is fit enough to factor.

With only six runners and a single front-runner, the field is likely to race in a tight bunch for much of the trip; any horse that gets shuffled back at a crucial flight or loses its position on the approach to the home straight could find recovery very difficult in such a small, potentially compressed field.

races.name: Thorn Plant Hire Beginners Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Ballystone
runners_data.note: Won over 2m at Killarney on Good 20 days ago and stays further — a natural hold-up operator whose closing style may be compromised if unable to get the rear berth in a field with multiple closers.|
runners_data.comment: Ballystone won three starts back and returns on a quick enough turnaround of 20 days with experience of both today's trip and going in his favour, giving him a solid platform to threaten; the main risk is that he has been out of the frame in his two subsequent starts.

runners_data.name: Fort Dino
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's five-year-old has been off 112 days and wears a hood; showed he handles Good going with a hurdling win over 18f on Heavy, and a prominent style suits a steady gallop.|
runners_data.comment: Fort Dino won two starts back but comes here ranked seventh of eight on our figures, has been off the track for 112 days, and carries a hefty 166 lb — a combination that makes him a tough sell despite that recent success.

runners_data.name: Happy Me
runners_data.note: Wearing a hood and last seen 7 days ago, this horse has failed to beat many rivals in recent outings but is in form by frequency; a naturally hold-up style horse crowded into midfield means the race shape may not suit.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, including a pulled-up effort in recent outings, Happy Me is ranked last on our figures and faces a stiff ask here, though he has run over today's going before and returns on a quick turnaround just seven days since his last start.

runners_data.name: Heroes Rise
runners_data.note: 508 days off the track for Gordon Elliott's six-year-old is a major unknown, but form prior to the break was solid (2-4-3-2-2 in last five with RPR experience) and the hold-up profile could thrive if the front two combust.|
runners_data.comment: Heroes Rise has been consistently competitive in recent starts, finishing placed three times in his last five, and has run over today's trip and going — yet 508 days off the track is a significant fitness question for this 166 lb burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Lemmy Caution
runners_data.note: Elliott's five-year-old front-runner has won over 24f on Good and finished second last time out; if he is allowed an uncontested lead he can prove stubborn, but Affinity Rock will test his resolve immediately.|
runners_data.comment: Placed third two starts back and a winner three starts back, Lemmy Caution arrives here 37 days on from his most recent run, carrying 166 lb, with experience of today's trip and going in his favour but our rating of 111, ranking him sixth of eight, suggests he faces a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Themanintheanorak
runners_data.note: Consistent in recent outings despite a series of sixth-place finishes, and a prominent style puts him in the right position structurally; his trainer has a modest record (0/2 in 14 days) and form figures don't inspire confidence.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and a consistent sixth in four of them, Themanintheanorak at least arrives fit on 20 days' rest with distance and going experience to call on, though his inability to convert that consistency into something better is the obvious concern under 166 lb.

runners_data.name: Where's My Jet
runners_data.note: Mullins runner with a hot trainer (11/26 in 14 days) but form reads 60P-00, including pulls-up and double-figure finishes; the class angle is appealing but output has been poor and a 20-day break doesn't resolve the form slump.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, including a pull-up two runs back, Where's My Jet arrives on a workable 20-day break with distance and going experience in his favour; a trainer firing at 42% over the past fortnight offers the strongest case for a turnaround.

runners_data.name: Affinity Rock
runners_data.note: Highest-rated runner (OR 124) and the lighter weight (159lbs vs 166lbs) could be an advantage at the fences; two consecutive second places on Good show he is consistent, but Collins's trainer strike rate is 0/9 in 14 days.|
runners_data.comment: Twice runner-up in her last two starts suggests she's knocking on the door, but 91 days off the track and a hefty 159 lb to carry are significant hurdles, and our rating of 114 leaves her trailing the principals.

races.paceDynamic: Affinity Rock and Lemmy Caution are the two confirmed front-runners and will both press for the lead from the outset over this extended 2m7½f trip at Killarney, creating a genuine contested gallop rather than a dawdle. Affinity Rock carries the higher OR (124) and has strong recent form (10-22), while Lemmy Caution showed enough last time to suggest he won't surrender the initiative cheaply, meaning the early sectionals will be honest rather than manufactured. The field contains more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate — Happy Me and Ballystone are genuine closers by preference but are mapped to midfield given that several true rear-runners are competing for limited space behind a strong pace, meaning they may race closer than ideal. Over this distance on Good ground with a genuine early gallop, prominent racers who can travel smoothly in behind the leaders and pick up efficiently will be best placed — pure hold-up horses face an uphill task if they cannot get their natural position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Affinity Rock and Lemmy Caution fight for the front and set an honest gallop that stretches the field from early.
scenarios.body: The sustained pace suits a horse travelling prominently who can stalk the leaders over the long Killarney circuit and assert in the straight; Fort Dino and Themanintheanorak are best placed to exploit if either front-runner cracks.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Affinity Rock asserts unchallenged and Lemmy Caution either fails to go with them or fades after the early duel.
scenarios.body: A dominant front-runner who controls tempo and jumps cleanly can steal a march on this field, especially if rivals sit too comfortably in midfield and cede the initiative.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Late
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners set a truly scorching gallop that burns them out, leaving late ground for closers.
scenarios.body: Heroes Rise is the one genuine hold-up horse with strong form figures (2-4-3-2 at trips and going matching today) and represents the main threat from off the pace; Ballystone also carries strong claims if able to find clear running.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If there are jumping errors or fallers at a crucial stage that scramble the order and allow an unexpected horse to inherit a clear lead.
scenarios.body: Where's My Jet or Themanintheanorak could benefit passively from attrition in a beginners' steeplechase where jumping errors are a real risk; Affinity Rock's lighter weight (159lbs) may aid agility at the fences.

watchPoints.text: Affinity Rock and Lemmy Caution will battle directly for the lead from the start — watch the first two fences closely to see who submits, as the loser of that duel may fade leaving the other with a soft lead.

Heroes Rise returns after 508 days off; watch for any signs of ring-rustiness or jumping errors at the early fences — if it travels sweetly it becomes a serious factor, but a long absence at a beginners' chase is a live risk.
Fort Dino's headgear (hood) is noted on a horse returning from 112 days off — watch for early keenness or erratic jumping that could undermine a naturally prominent style.

In a beginners' steeplechase on Good ground, watch the fence at the top of the hill where the track turns — this is a common site for errors as inexperienced chasers adjust; Happy Me and Themanintheanorak have the least convincing recent form and could be most vulnerable here.

Where's My Jet's Mullins booking (Brian Hayes) is the sharpest jockey upgrade in the race — watch if it is positioned closer to the pace than its hold-up form implies, which could signal a tactical change.

races.name: Easyfix Equine Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Oneforgonzo
runners_data.note: Hold-up galloper who showed clear ability when winning over Good 20f, but this 23f trip on today's evidence is a stretch; apprentice claim helps at the weights and recent 12-day turnaround is fine, with sim-going record a reasonable 6 from 15.
runners_data.comment: Oneforgonzo won four starts back and arrives here fit on a twelve-day turnaround, with experience of both today's trip and going in his favour; he carries 168 lb but his overall profile makes him our pick ahead of the top-rated runner.

runners_data.name: Smallcraftwarning
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up type whose sim-going record of 0W from 15 attempts flags a frustrating inability to convert; 18 days since last run and tongue-tie fitted, but 15 outings without a win at similar trips on similar ground is a significant red flag for winning potential.
runners_data.comment: Smallcraftwarning arrives fresh enough on 18 days' rest, has run over today's trip and going, and his second four starts back underlines he can compete at this level — though winless in his last six starts, that consistency risk remains the one concern.

runners_data.name: King Ferdinand
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner and race-shaper, but his recent form reads 66/P0P and he is arguably racing out of his natural role over this 23f trip compared to his usual 20f assignments; STYLE_FIT flag reflects the concern that dictating here may cost him at the business end.
runners_data.comment: King Ferdinand has run over today's trip and going and, rated 105 and ranked top of this field, he shapes as a leading threat despite carrying 166 lb; the main concern is his two pulled-up efforts in recent starts, leaving his current wellbeing open to question.

runners_data.name: Kilkee Bay
runners_data.note: Ran second and won at Killarney-type distances on Good and Soft, and the blinkers fitted sharpens his jumping focus; seven-year-old lightly raced hold-up type whose sim-going record of 0W2P at similar Going leaves the winning question open, though a clean round here would put him competitive late.
runners_data.comment: Kilkee Bay won three starts back and was second two starts back, so carries some recent form into this, and he has run over today's trip and going before; but a fifth last time out and a lofty 163 lb on his back are hurdles to clear.

runners_data.name: Western Model
runners_data.note: Won over 24f on Good recently — the most relevant piece of form on the card for this trip and Going combination; hold-up style and 45-day freshener combine well, and trainer T14 strike rate of 1/5 is modest but the form speaks for itself.
runners_data.comment: Western Model arrives here as a winner last time out and has experience of both today's trip and going, making him a strong each-way candidate at 162 lb; the fitness query after a 45-day absence is the one thing punters must weigh up.

runners_data.name: Je Suis
runners_data.note: Blinkers-fitted prominent racer who has placed at 26f on Good and looks set to challenge for a forward berth behind King Ferdinand; 28-day absence is straightforward, though 0W1P in similar conditions and a recent string including pulled-up runs tempers expectations.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked eighth of thirteen, Je Suis does at least bring distance and going experience to the table and returns on a fresh 28-day break, though 158 lb is a stiff burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Ladies Well
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse repositioned in the mapping because this field has too many closers to fit truthfully at the rear — her last two completed runs include a win at 23f on Good and a second, and the tongue-tie is retained; Darragh O'Keeffe's booking is a strong positive, though the STYLE_FIT tag signals she may not reproduce that form if unable to settle into her preferred position.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 12 of 13 on our figures, Ladies Well faces a stiff ask off 158 lb with her trainer badly out of form at 1/22 in the past fortnight; she has run over today's trip and going before, and a win two starts back at least shows she can find the front.

runners_data.name: Walk Away Harry
runners_data.note: Flagged as fading in the finish and his best recent placing is a fourth on identical Good ground over only 19f — this 23f trip is a clear concern; 80 days off the track is the longest absence in the field, and the redistribution means he is unlikely to get the cover and late-race space his hold-up style demands.
runners_data.comment: Walk Away Harry has run over today's going before but arrives 80 days between runs and is yet to win in his last five starts, which dims confidence; carrying 158 lb is a further ask, though our rating of 97 suggests there may be more to find.

runners_data.name: Wakey Wakey Man
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with promise — ran second at 20f on Soft and third at 23f on Good — but has not raced in 99 days, the biggest layoff here; his true closer profile is squeezed by the field's pace composition, and a STYLE_FIT discount applies if he cannot get back to his natural ground.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and now absent for 99 days, Wakey Wakey Man faces a stiff ask ranked tenth of thirteen on our figures, though he has run over today's trip and going before and a third two starts back offers a sliver of encouragement.

runners_data.name: Mount Shenshan
runners_data.note: Danny Mullins takes the ride which is a clear positive, but the recent form reads 5-3560 and his best outings have been at 22-26f on Good; his hold-up style is genuine and the redistribution note reflects that he simply cannot drift as wide as he would like with this many closers in behind.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Mount Shenshan does at least bring distance and going experience to this, and a rating of 90 offers some encouragement, though a top weight of 155 lb and her unplaced latest run make the case against her a tough one to ignore.

runners_data.name: Tropical Image
runners_data.note: Trainer has saddled two winners in the last 14 days from six runners — the best immediate form of any handler here; the horse's own form is modest (best recently a second at 19f on Good), and as a natural closer mapped forward the STYLE_FIT tag limits confidence, though the stable form is worth tracking.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 11th of 13 on our figures, Tropical Image is hard to fancy at the weights carrying 155 lb; the second two starts back is a mild plus, and she has run over today's trip and going before, but the overall profile makes her difficult to support.

runners_data.name: Cullenwaine
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing eight-year-old who won last time out at 23f on Good and has four placings from five runs at similar distances and Going — the form profile is tailor-made for today's race shape; the 3lb claim from Shane O'Callaghan offsets any small weight concern and blinkers fitted throughout his recent form.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Cullenwaine faces a stiff ask off 152 lb, and a mixed sequence of fourth, fifth and two runner-up efforts before that recent win gives little encouragement, though he has experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Malton Groove
runners_data.note: Has placed at 23-24f on Good three times from 15 sim-going outings but without a win; the 34-day break is straightforward, tongue-tie and hood fitted, but his redistribution from true hold-up means he cannot realistically get the patient, wide-swinging run he needs in a field this size.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Malton Groove does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and a third and second in recent starts suggest he can hit the frame; however, a hefty 150 lb burden and a ranking of seventh of thirteen make progress hard to envisage.

races.paceDynamic: King Ferdinand is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with only Je Suis and Cullenwaine willing to race prominently, faces minimal pressure in a 13-runner field over 2m7½f on Good ground at Killarney. With no genuine rival to challenge him early, King Ferdinand can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop that plays directly into the hands of horses travelling smoothly just off the pace rather than those forced wide or stuck in traffic at the rear. The field contains a significant overhang of hold-up types — Walk Away Harry, Ladies Well, Wakey Wakey Man, Mount Shenshan, Tropical Image and Malton Groove are all natural closers compressed into a midfield cluster because the race shape simply cannot accommodate them all at the back; the prominent slots will most realistically be claimed by Je Suis and Cullenwaine. A well-judged, uncontested pace in this stamp of race over this trip on Good ground strongly favours prominent and patient-midfield runners who travel into the contest smoothly and pounce between the final two fences rather than those needing a truly honest gallop to get competitive.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: King Ferdinand Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If King Ferdinand bowls along at a measured clip unchallenged and the pace is steady enough that prominent travellers conserve energy for the last mile.
scenarios.body: Je Suis and Cullenwaine track the front-runner in a perfect position, while the genuine closers are caught in a bottleneck and cannot generate momentum from deep; a horse with jumping fluency and a prominent berth picks up decisively at the last.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the moderate gallop set by King Ferdinand causes the race to bunch and a sustained end-to-end duel emerges between the final four fences.
scenarios.body: With horses compressed together from the home turn, a runner with a good jump at the penultimate fence and class in hand can surge clear; this benefits the horse with better form credentials that has been cruising through the race in third or fourth.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver Staying Surge
scenarios.trigger: If King Ferdinand's pace proves deceptively strong enough to string the field out and the closers find clear daylight on the long run to the last.
scenarios.body: This is the scenario where genuine hold-up types can thread through on the outside and pick off tiring leaders late, particularly those with proven stamina at this trip; however, most of the nominal closers are redistributed from their natural style and may lack the positional discipline to execute.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Flatters To Deceive
scenarios.trigger: If King Ferdinand is eventually run out of it turning for home having set a pace that proves too hot for his limited recent form, creating a muddled finish.
scenarios.body: A horse whose jockey has tracked the leader close enough to inherit the lead briefly but is then caught by a fresher rival charging through; this scenario is unlikely given King Ferdinand's confirmed lead role and the shallow pace rivalry behind him.

watchPoints.text: King Ferdinand's jumping — if he makes a significant error at any of the first five fences he will lose his uncontested lead and the entire race shape collapses, benefiting Je Suis and Cullenwaine who are poised just behind.

Walk Away Harry carries a 80-day layoff and a fading-in-finish flag — watch his movement in the parade ring and whether Philip Byrnes elects to try to ride him handier than his mapped position suggests, which would further congest the prominent berths.

The cluster of redistributed closers — Wakey Wakey Man, Mount Shenshan, Tropical Image and Malton Groove — will be competing for the same late ground on the inner; watch for traffic problems turning out of the back straight where Killarney's layout forces a concertina effect.

Western Model's freshness angle after 45 days off is the most obvious market mover to track — if he drifts in the ring it suggests connections have a doubt; if he shortens despite his hold-up style in a slow-run race, that jockey Donagh Meyler has been briefed to ride more positively than the profile implies.

Cullenwaine's early position is the key tactical read — if Shane O'Callaghan gets him into second or third behind King Ferdinand within the first mile, this race shape sets up perfectly for him and the market will likely reflect that from the home turn.

races.name: Brehon Hotel & Spa Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Illtakehimmyself
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with solid recent form (two seconds and a win in last four), well-suited to good ground with a 6/9 strike-rate in similar conditions; Calum Hogan (5lb claim) keeps the weight competitive and 35 days since last run looks ideal, but needs more pace than Ollie La Ba Ba alone is likely to generate.|
runners_data.comment: Ran over today's trip and going, and a winner last time out, Illtakehimmyself has placed in three of his other four recent starts too; carrying 166 lb against stronger company, though, and our rating of 103 suggests he faces a stiff ask here.

runners_data.name: Kings Jet
runners_data.note: Raced 12 days ago and has shown consistency at this level, with a win and two placings in seven runs on good ground; a natural hold-up horse who will need the pace to be honest to reel in those ahead, and stepping back up to 2m5f from shorter trips is the key stamina question.|
runners_data.comment: Kings Jet returns in good heart after a runner-up finish last time out, and has experience of today's going, but his interrupted recent sequence — which includes an unseating and a pull-up — leaves him winless in his last five starts, making the 166 lb he carries a further ask.

runners_data.name: Gaelic Des Chastys
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old with excellent recent form — five placings or wins from five in similar going — returning from 203 days off which is the chief concern; Patrick O'Brien's 5lb claim helps the dead weight and the horse's record over 2m-plus on good ground is genuinely strong.|
runners_data.comment: Gaelic Des Chastys has been placed in four of his last five starts, including a win, and has run over today's trip and going, yet he arrives 203 days off the track carrying 162 lb and our rating ranks him well adrift of the principals.

runners_data.name: Ollie La Ba Ba
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner here and likely to get a soft lead, but a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.91 reflects that this is not its sharpest profile — form in the last six runs shows five sixths and a single win, and the trainer has sent out 2 winners from 6 runners in the past 14 days which provides some stable confidence.|
runners_data.comment: Ollie La Ba Ba showed he can win at this level when scoring four starts back, and he has experience of both today's trip and conditions; the concern is a return from 73 days off and a hefty 161 lb to carry.

runners_data.name: Burru
runners_data.note: Ran just 7 days ago which is the obvious flag, but has won on this course over 2m on good ground and the 15/15 good-going record underlines suitability to conditions; a naturally prominent racer who should be prominent early and is likely to be the most meaningful threat to the leader.|
runners_data.comment: Burru returns just seven days after his last outing, so fitness is not in question, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions. A winner three starts back, he was fourth last time out, and our rating of 108 puts him comfortably above his official figure of 100.

runners_data.name: Tippin And Tappin
runners_data.note: Two wins from four career starts on good ground and genuinely progressive, but holds up in races by nature — squeezed into a midfield mapping here because the field is loaded with similar types; the STYLE_FIT tag (0.93) means its chance depends partly on whether it can push forward from its usual rear berth.|
runners_data.comment: Two successive wins in recent starts offer some encouragement, but a pull-up last time and a rating of 93 ranked bottom of this field make him very hard to fancy, even if he has experience of today's going and returns after a 34-day break.

runners_data.name: Toon Town
runners_data.note: Won over 2m on good ground and has placed at this course, giving it genuine positional and surface credentials; a true hold-up horse that has been redistributed to midfield, and Shane O'Callaghan's 3lb claim is a small but relevant assist — likely to be closer to the pace than its natural style dictates.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom but one on our figures, Toon Town carries a hefty 159 lb and was beaten into seventh last time out, making him hard to fancy here, though he has winning form in recent starts and has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Seeitoldya
runners_data.note: A young five-year-old with no wins or places from eight similar-going runs, which is the starkest negative in this field; Harry Sexton's 7lb claim softens the burden but this horse's natural hold-up style has been redistributed forward, and the recent form string of 5-U-0-6-P does not inspire confidence at this level.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and pulled up most recently, Seeitoldya arrives with little to inspire confidence despite having run over today's trip and going before; a trainer without a winner in 20 attempts over the past fortnight is a further drag on his prospects.

runners_data.name: Shannon Bank
runners_data.note: Won over 2m on good ground and has placed twice in similar conditions, giving a reasonable profile, but has been nudged into a midfield mapping from a true hold-up role and the last five runs include three sevenths; Donagh Meyler rides and 51 days since last run is a minor concern.|
runners_data.comment: Shannon Bank won two starts back but has since finished seventh and is now 51 days absent, which tempers confidence; she has run over today's distance and going before and carries 158 lb off an official mark of 99, leaving her with something to prove on recent evidence.

runners_data.name: Miners Bridge
runners_data.note: Phillip Enright takes the ride on a horse with two placings from five runs on good ground over 2m-plus trips; naturally prominent and likely to sit just off Ollie La Ba Ba, making this a genuinely favourable race shape for its style — consistent rather than spectacular form.|
runners_data.comment: Runners-up two starts back and carrying a hefty 157 lb, Miners Bridge has strong claims on a rating of 108, and his experience over today's trip and going underlines his fitness as a genuine threat after just 17 days off — though the main risk is that he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Ferdia
runners_data.note: A ten-year-old carrying the lowest OR in the field at 82, with no wins or places from eight runs on good ground; naturally a hold-up horse whose true rear position has been redistributed to midfield, and recent form of 9-6-8-7-0 gives little reason to expect improvement over this trip.|
runners_data.comment: Ferdia catches the eye on our ratings, ranked top of the field, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions; the concern is a winless run of form across his last five starts that he must snap.

races.paceDynamic: Ollie La Ba Ba is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner handicap chase over 2m5f at Killarney, and on good ground with no genuine pace rival to challenge her, she is set to bowl along at a comfortable, uncontested tempo from the outset. Burru and Miners Bridge will press into prominent positions behind, but neither is likely to apply sustained early pressure on the leader, meaning the gallop should be honest rather than brutal — enough to string the field out over the fences but not enough to cause carnage up front. This race shape, with one controlled pace-setter and a clutch of hold-up horses being shuffled into midfield against their nature, strongly favours horses that can travel prominently in the slipstream of Ollie La Ba Ba and pounce from a close enough position in the straight, rather than true closers who need a strong pace to make up ground. Several runners flagged as redistributed — including Toon Town, Tippin And Tappin, Shannon Bank, Seeitoldya and Ferdia — are genuine hold-up types who are unlikely to secure their natural rear position given the volume of similar styles in the field; of these, Toon Town and Tippin And Tappin are the most likely to push forward and actually race closer than their mapping suggests.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ollie La Ba Ba Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Ollie La Ba Ba is allowed to dictate a steady, uncontested gallop and the field fails to organise any meaningful pursuit.
scenarios.body: Ollie La Ba Ba bowls along in front, jumping confidently and setting a rhythm that suits her stamina; the lack of a pressing rival means she conserves energy and has reserves left for the final climb.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Burru or Miners Bridge press Ollie La Ba Ba sufficiently to soften her and one of the prominent-tracking pair outstays her on the run-in.
scenarios.body: A modest but consistent gallop keeps the prominent horses in contention throughout, and any slight fade from the leader after the last fence opens the door for a close-travelling rival to collar her.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough — aided by Toon Town or Tippin And Tappin racing closer than expected — to set up a true staying finish that rewards a big run from off the pace.
scenarios.body: A competitive early tempo opens ground for a horse held up in rear to sweep through beaten rivals on the long Killarney run-in; the good ground and 2m5f trip would amplify the finishing effort.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse And Melee
scenarios.trigger: If Ollie La Ba Ba sets too slow a gallop, bunching the field and causing a messy scramble for position over the fences with multiple interference incidents.
scenarios.body: Crowded jumping leads to errors and shuffling, putting a premium on a horse that travels smoothly through the chaos and finds daylight early in the straight; a horse with clean jumping credentials benefits most.

watchPoints.text: Ollie La Ba Ba sets the entire pace structure — watch whether she is allowed to bowl along unchallenged from the outset or if Burru and Miners Bridge apply enough pressure to compromise her stamina in the final mile.
Burru ran only 7 days ago; monitor market moves and watch in the paddock for any signs of fatigue or stiffness that could undermine what looks like a genuinely favourable position in the race shape.

Toon Town and Tippin And Tappin are both natural hold-up horses who may attempt to race more prominently than usual given the field composition — if either takes a position close to the pace early, it reshapes the entire midfield dynamic.

Gaelic Des Chastys returns from 203 days off and Patrick O'Brien's 5lb claim is important for feasibility at OR 103; watch the market for any significant support that would indicate the yard is confident the horse is race-fit.|

The weight cluster between OR 99–107 is extremely tight across nine of the eleven runners, meaning small advantages in position, jumping accuracy and jockey decision-making at the fences are likely to be decisive — watch for any jumping errors at the open ditch that could compromise race-shape dependent runners.|

races.name: Gallivan Financial Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Crowsatedappletart
runners_data.note: Has won over this exact course and distance on good ground (1/19f/SOF, 1/16f/GOO) and travels prominently; claiming rider Michael Kenneally (5lb) is the minor concern, but tp headgear and strong sim-going record (12/15) are positives at OR 123.
runners_data.comment: Crowsatedappletart won two starts back but has posted sixth-place efforts either side of that success, and a hefty 166 lb burden is the obvious concern today; he has run over today's trip and going before, though our rating of 114 suggests he faces a stiff task against stronger rivals.

runners_data.name: Femme Magnifique
runners_data.note: Trainer David Harry Kelly in form (1/12 T14), mare has won twice on good ground and finished 1-2-1 in last three starts; races prominently and arrives fresh on 34 days, her trip range and going record (10/15) suit perfectly.
runners_data.comment: Femme Magnifique arrives on the back of a win last time out, and a further win three starts back, with experience over today's trip and going working in her favour; the chief concern is a demanding 164 lb on her back.

runners_data.name: War Correspondent
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type with the deepest similar-going experience in the field (14/15) but form string (44U439) shows consistency concerns; a 7lb claimer in Harry Sexton adds some risk and the tb headgear hints at a tendency to pull, which could hurt in a steady-paced race.
runners_data.comment: Shaped with promise when third two starts back, and War Correspondent has run over today's trip and going, arriving here in decent nick just 18 days on; winless in recent starts and a trainer in the depths of a cold spell give slight pause, but his rating of 125 marks him as the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Costacurta
runners_data.note: De Bromhead yard in fine form (4/38 T14), he is the sole confirmed front-runner and can dictate every yard on good ground (7/8 sim-going); his second-half-of-race jumping at fences will be critical — if he gets tired and makes errors late, the prominent horses catch him.
runners_data.comment: Costacurta has shown consistent placing ability in recent starts, finishing second and twice third in his last five, and returns after 27 days looking fit; he has run over today's trip and going, though his inability to convert in recent starts remains the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Beauforts Storm
runners_data.note: Races from hold-up, has one win and four places from 12 similar-going runs; lightly weighted at 155lbs and fresh enough on 29 days, but a string that reads 772U74 does not scream confidence, and the 5lb claimer O'Sullivan adds an element of inexperience.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Beauforts Storm does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and a return two starts back offers some encouragement, though a weight of 155 lb and patchy recent form — including an unseating — give cause for caution.

runners_data.name: Stuntman Steve
runners_data.note: Cromwell yard active (5/16 T14), but form of 55-PU5 includes a pulled-up run and this hold-up type's sim-going record (11/15, 1W) is modest; the b headgear is first-time equipment and could sharpen him, worth monitoring in-running but not a natural winner of the likely shape.
runners_data.comment: Ranked second of nine on our ratings and proven in conditions, Stuntman Steve brings strong claims on a pound-for-pound basis at 155 lb, though his recent record — winless in his last five starts and including an unseating — is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Kilbrin Rocco
runners_data.note: Won on identical course and distance (1/16f/GOO) in recent form and races prominently, making him one of the better-placed tactical fits in this shape; trainer McCarthy has two winners from six (T14) and the t headgear is established equipment — the OR drop to 105 could prove lenient.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Kilbrin Rocco is hard to fancy after finishing ninth last time out, and his recent form is patchy at best, though he has run over today's distance and going before and showed he can win in this grade a couple of starts back.

runners_data.name: Ballybrittas
runners_data.note: In fine recent form (3-1-5 last three) and carries strong sim-going stats (11/12, 2W5P), but his true hold-up style means he is racing out of his natural position in this shape; Shane O'Callaghan (3lb) is a positive booking, though the tactical compromise tempers confidence regardless of raw ability.
runners_data.comment: Ballybrittas has shown he can win at this level — a winner two starts back — but finishes of fifth and seventh in his last four starts around that success paint an inconsistent picture, and ranked eighth of nine on our figures he faces a stiff ask at 147 lb.

runners_data.name: Piccolo Player
runners_data.note: Youngest in the field at five, has placed three times on good ground without winning (0W3P sim-going); a natural rear-of-field type squeezed into a midfield role by the redistribution, which blunts his best asset — coming from off a strong pace — making this a difficult shape for him to win.
runners_data.comment: Piccolo Player has shown consistency without ever threatening to take the prize, and with our rating placing him seventh of nine runners here, he is hard to fancy at the weights — though he comes into this fit off a 16-day break, has run over today's trip and going before, and was third last time out.

races.paceDynamic: Costacurta is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, Darragh O'Keeffe can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from flag to finish over 2m1f on good ground at Killarney. Crowsatedappletart and Femme Magnifique will press forward into prominent positions just off the pace, with Kilbrin Rocco also likely to race up with the pace group, meaning the front half of the field will be well populated. The field holds more hold-up types than the rear of the race can naturally accommodate — Ballybrittas and Piccolo Player are genuine closers but will find themselves shuffled into a midfield role rather than their true rearward position, which compromises their ability to produce a late run from off a strong gallop. With Costacurta controlling a measured pace and prominent types in close attendance, this race shape most strongly favours horses that can race within a length or two of the leader and quicken when it matters — the prominent-racing profile is the one to be on.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Costacurta Controls, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Costacurta dictates an uncontested, measured pace and prominent horses travel smoothly throughout.
scenarios.body: O'Keeffe pings the early fences cleanly, sets a fair but not punishing tempo, and the winner emerges from the group just off the pace in the straight. Crowsatedappletart and Femme Magnifique, both proven at this trip on good ground, are ideally placed to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Leader Runs Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Costacurta meets every fence well and the chasing pack is unable to sustain the gallop in the straight.
scenarios.body: With no one able to close, O'Keeffe's front-runner simply lengthens from the last and the race is over before the finish line; his good-ground form record (7 from 8 similar conditions) underpins this scenario. Prominent horses who have used too much petrol trying to stay in touch are left for dead.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Weaves Through
scenarios.trigger: If Costacurta sets a genuinely strong pace that strings the field out and creates a gap for a midfield runner to weave through.
scenarios.body: War Correspondent, who has the most similar-going experience of the hold-up brigade, could benefit if the pace is stronger than anticipated and the prominent horses wilt; Beauforts Storm is also capable of finding a pocket from midfield. This shape requires a faster-than-expected tempo to materialise, which is not the most likely outcome given the lone front-runner's natural tendency to conserve.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is unexpectedly strong and the race falls apart late, allowing true hold-up runners to deliver from the rear.
scenarios.body: This scenario depends on Ballybrittas and Piccolo Player producing their natural closing style, but both are mapped out of their true role in this shape and are unlikely to find themselves far enough back to generate a meaningful late run. The low probability reflects the redistribution penalty — genuine late-closers simply cannot recapture their best tactical position when the field is this congested at the rear.

watchPoints.text: Costacurta's jumping under pressure — if he makes a significant error at any of the fences from halfway, the entire race dynamic flips instantly and the prominent pack (Crowsatedappletart, Femme Magnifique) inherit the race on straightforward terms.

Kilbrin Rocco's early position — if G B Noonan pushes forward aggressively, the front group becomes crowded and Costacurta may not get the clean, uncontested lead that underpins Scenario A, elevating the chance of a more contested and ultimately faster pace.

Ballybrittas freshness factor — on just 12 days since last run with two recent wins, he arrives in career-best form; if O'Callaghan manages to slot him handier than his natural style dictates, the redistribution penalty shrinks and his raw ability becomes dangerous.

War Correspondent's jumping — the tb headgear and a U (unseated) in recent form raises a flag at the fences; if he jumps cleanly and Harry Sexton (7lb) can hold a prominent enough position, his vast similar-going experience (14/15) could see him in the mix late.

races.name: Peadar's Pub Glenbeigh Flat Race

runners_data.name: Con Did It
runners_data.note: Lightly raced six-year-old for Eoin Christopher McCarthy whose running style is genuinely unknown, making placement on the pace map speculative; the 7lb-claiming Mr J Dunne adds further uncertainty, and days-since-last-run data is absent, so watch for market moves as the primary guide.
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and making his debut, Con Did It arrives without a form line to read but that very inexperience leaves plenty of improvement on the table; carrying 168 lb is the immediate challenge for a gelding whose ceiling remains entirely unknown.

runners_data.name: Stary Notions
runners_data.note: Another lightly raced six-year-old with no disclosed style, trained by P M Lynch who shows no recent runners in the T14 window; Mr R W Barron's 5lb claim is useful but form evidence is too thin to identify a tactical role with confidence.
runners_data.comment: Stary Notions makes his debut carrying 168 lb, entirely unexposed and open to improvement — a blank slate whose potential remains untapped with everything still to learn.

runners_data.name: Suresuresure
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for John F O'Neill whose recent form string (8P-075) is uninspiring and who carries a pattern of fading in the finish — 45 days off the track on good ground over the full 2m1f trip is a combination that demands caution rather than confidence.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and pulling up on one occasion, Suresuresure does at least bring distance experience and a solid speed rating of 88 to the table, though the weight burden of 168 lb looks the chief obstacle to reversing his recent struggles.

runners_data.name: The Last Line
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who ran a promising second on good ground over a similar trip — his only career start — making him interesting on style and going compatibility, though 776 days off the track for the Kiely yard is a significant fitness concern that cannot be ignored.
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement, The Last Line was runner-up last time out — his only recent start — and returns after a lengthy absence of over two years carrying 168 lb, with plenty still to find out about him.

runners_data.name: Iron Sword
runners_data.note: Prominent-going four-year-old for Andrew Slattery who has shown placed form on good ground and is only 16 days since last run, suggesting freshness; two runs into his career he has yet to win but his style suits tracking Walkineezy closely.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out and winless in recent starts, Iron Sword nonetheless heads the ratings and a run just 16 days ago keeps him fit; carrying 165 lb for a trainer in lean current form are the notes of caution against a profile that otherwise demands respect.

runners_data.name: Rocky Alfonso
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with just one run, finished fourth on soft, for the powerful S Curling yard with Derek O'Connor — a top amateur — in the plate; unknown style in races means his tactical role is unclear, but the jockey booking is the most notable positive angle.
runners_data.comment: Rocky Alfonso was fourth last time out and, carrying 165 lb on just 16 days' rest, he arrives fresh and third on our ratings on a rating of 95; the concern is that he remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Walkineezy
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed pace-setter in the race, trained by Denis Gerard Hogan (2/27 T14 strike-rate) and ridden by Mr H C Swan; the STYLE_FIT flag notes this horse may be operating outside its most comfortable role, so while it will likely lead, its chance of winning having done the donkey work should be tempered accordingly.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last two starts and ranked fifth of nine on our figures, Walkineezy is hard to fancy at the weights, carrying 165 lb, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns after a 24-day break.

runners_data.name: Killeedy
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for the Willie Mullins/Patrick Mullins combination — always a yard worth respecting — with tongue tie noted and one run on good ground behind it; a steady pace set by Walkineezy is not ideal for a genuine hold-up style, but the trainer angle keeps it relevant.
runners_data.comment: Killeedy has run over today's trip and going, and a trainer firing at 42% in the last fortnight gives her strong support off the back of a 34-day freshener, but she heads into this yet to score in recent starts and must convert that promise under a hefty 161 lb.

runners_data.name: Streamhill
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer for Padraig Butler whose form shows a string of fourth and fifth placings on good ground over 16f — honest but not a winner; 66 days since last run and a modest pace scenario both work against her securing a first career success here.
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and yet to win in her last four starts, Streamhill returns after 66 days carrying 161 lb, but that consistent run of fifths and a fourth hints at a mare still finding her feet and open to better.

races.paceDynamic: Walkineezy is the lone confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner flat race over 2m1f on good ground at Killarney, and with no other runner carrying a lead style, the pace is set to be controlled and uncontested from the outset. The prominent types — The Last Line and Iron Sword — will slot in behind without any pressure to force the issue, meaning Walkineezy can dictate a measured, sustainable gallop throughout. Hold-up horses Suresuresure, Killeedy, and Streamhill will be further back, relying on the pace not collapsing too early, while the unknown-style runners Con Did It and Stary Notions add uncertainty to the mid-race shape. With a single unhurried front-runner setting a steady tempo on good turf, this race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can track the leader into the straight and produce a finishing effort without needing a true pace injection — hold-up horses face the additional risk of a modest gallop leaving them with too little ground to make up late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Walkineezy Dictates, Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Walkineezy sets a controlled, unchallenged pace and a prominent tracker produces the best turn-of-foot in the straight.
scenarios.body: Walkineezy bowls along at a sustainable clip with The Last Line and Iron Sword tucked in close, and when the pace quickens approaching the final turn, the best-placed prominent racer drives through to score. This shape is tailor-made for horses who travel smoothly close to the pace without burning energy early on good ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is slightly stronger than expected and closers get a genuine target to aim at in the home straight.
scenarios.body: Killeedy or Streamhill are held up quietly off the even tempo, and if Walkineezy sets just enough pace to string the field out, a well-timed late run from the back gives the finishers a chance. Killeedy in particular is interesting given the W P Mullins/P W Mullins combination, though good ground and a modest gallop are not ideal for true hold-up reliance.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Unknown Runners Blind-Side Field
scenarios.trigger: If one of Con Did It or Stary Notions carries natural front-running or prominent ability that transforms the race dynamic once underway.
scenarios.body: A lightly-raced runner with an undisclosed style races prominently from the outset and disrupts Walkineezy's uncontested lead, injecting a pace dimension the market hadn't anticipated. In that scenario, horses with tactical versatility who handle a quicker early tempo gain an edge, and the race becomes more genuinely test of stamina over the 2m1f trip on good turf.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closer Outstays
scenarios.trigger: If Walkineezy's gallop is truly pedestrian and the race turns into a sprint finish where stamina at a slow tempo decides the outcome.
scenarios.body: A falsely-run race bunches the field heading for home, and the horse who stays best over the full 2m1f when the pace suddenly quickens late scores, favouring those with proven stamina rather than pure speed. Suresuresure and Streamhill both have form over the trip but carry fade concerns that make this scenario unreliable for them specifically.

watchPoints.text: Watch Walkineezy's early sectionals — if Mr H C Swan is content to bowl along at a genuine pace, the race becomes strongly contestable for prominent trackers The Last Line and Iron Sword, but if the gallop is artificially slow, the entire pace scenario unravels.

Con Did It and Stary Notions are both complete unknowns stylistically; if either races prominently and tests Walkineezy from the front, the even-tempo assumption underpinning the dominant scenario is immediately compromised.

The Last Line returns from 776 days off the track — if the Kiely yard has him fit and fresh, his good-ground prominent style gives him a live each-way profile, but that absence makes pre-race confidence in him a leap of faith.

Killeedy carries the most powerful trainer-jockey combination in the race in W P Mullins and P W Mullins; even with hold-up style disadvantaged by the expected pace shape, the yard's ability to produce fit, well-prepared horses means any market drift deserves monitoring.

Rocky Alfonso's booking of Derek O'Connor is the strongest jockey engagement in the field for an unknown-style runner — watch where he positions early as it will clarify whether the horse has natural front-running tendencies that could alter the race map.
